holidays.name: National Gardening Exercise Day
holidays.description: A day that encourages people to get outside, dig in the dirt, and count weeding, raking, and planting as a legitimate workout. Your tomato plants are basically your personal trainers.
holidays.origin: Observed as an unofficial U.S. wellness holiday, listed in many national day calendars, promoting gardening as a healthy physical activity.
holidays.funFact: Gardening for about 30 to 45 minutes can burn roughly as many calories as a brisk walk or a light aerobics session.

holidays.name: National Yo-Yo Day
holidays.description: A day to dust off your yo-yo and attempt a 'Walk the Dog' or 'Around the World' without hitting yourself in the face.
holidays.origin: Celebrated on June 6 in the United States, honoring one of the world's oldest toys, which was popularized in America by Pedro Flores in the 1920s and later bought by Donald F. Duncan.
holidays.funFact: A yo-yo was reportedly taken aboard the Space Shuttle Discovery in 1985 to test how it behaves in zero gravity, and it can keep spinning in space.

holidays.name: National Drive-In Movie Day
holidays.description: A nostalgic celebration of watching films from the comfort of your car, complete with snacks, blankets, and questionable speaker hookups.
holidays.origin: Marks the anniversary of the first drive-in theater, opened by Richard Hollingshead in Camden, New Jersey, on June 6, 1933.
holidays.funFact: Hollingshead tested the idea by nailing a bedsheet to trees in his backyard and placing a projector on the hood of his car.

holidays.name: National Applesauce Cake Day
holidays.description: A day to celebrate the humble, moist, spiced cake made with applesauce, a dessert that lets you feel mildly virtuous while eating cake.
holidays.origin: A food holiday listed in national day calendars, tied to the old-fashioned American tradition of baking with applesauce as a substitute for scarce butter and eggs during lean times.
holidays.funFact: Applesauce cake recipes were popular during the Great Depression and wartime rationing because applesauce stretched scarce fats and sugar.

holidays.name: Russian Language Day
holidays.description: A United Nations observance honoring the Russian language, celebrated on the birthday of beloved poet Alexander Pushkin, often called the father of modern Russian literature.
holidays.origin: Established by the UN in 2010 to promote multilingualism and cultural diversity, with June 6 chosen as Pushkin's birthday in 1799.
holidays.funFact: Russian has no verb for 'to be' in the present tense, so 'I am a teacher' is literally said as 'I teacher.'
